We also seek to attract culturally and academically diverse faculty who value working with diverse students. Salary The salary is commensurate with education and experience. Job Summary/Basic Function The Department of Accounting at Middle Tennessee State University invites applicants for a full-time, temporary (non-tenurable) faculty position at the rank of lecturer. This is a one-year temporary appointment. The contract may be renewed annually based on available funding, demonstrated need, and satisfactory performance as assessed by annual evaluations. The appointment start date is August 1, 2026. The Jennings A. Jones College of Business promotes a high-quality, student-centric teaching and learning model. The successful candidate will be diligent, creative, supportive, and adaptable to the ever-changing market. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following: Teaching a total of five courses each semester, both on-ground and online. Examples of courses that may be included are principles of accounting, survey of accounting, and auditing courses. A required training course offered by MTSU Online must be completed before teaching online courses. University service or research will not be required. Adapting courses for both on-ground and online formats, ensuring that the student experience is equivalent across modalities. Delivering high-quality instruction by planning and implementing effective learning strategies and environments, utilizing a variety of student engagement strategies in the classroom to ensure active student participation. Promoting student success through timely communication, grading, and feedback. Meeting professional expectations by maintaining professional currency and contributing to a collaborative culture across the College. Required Education Applicants must meet one of the following educational requirements: master’s degree in accounting master’s degree in management or business administration with fifteen (15) years of professional experience in accounting master’s degree in management or business administration with 18 graduate hours in accounting Bachelor of Science in Accounting, currently licensed as a Certified Public Accountant (CPA), and six (6) years of professional experience Other Desirables Applicants with the following will receive special consideration: Audit certifications such as Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) or Certified Internal Controls Auditor (CISA), or other related certifications. Work experience in internal or external audit. Prior teaching experience. Together, we enrich the lives of students, and their families; develop a talented workforce; and partner with our community to lead boldly into the future. Respect rights of students and access to educational opportunities. Counsel and advise students regarding academic preparation and career goals. Assist in formal and informal placement activities for employment and/or transfer to four-year institutions. Work to retain students. Provide out-of-class assistance to students. Support student activities. Maintain shop safety and supervise students in the scene shop. Organizational Culture Provide support in the Humanities and Fine Arts Division that aligns with the College’s values. Embrace and promote the College’s goals and support the Humanities and Fine Arts Division’s efforts to utilize best practices related to the student experience. Assist in recruitment and selection of college personnel as assigned. Participate in accreditation, assessment, and performance funding processes. Support and participate in college/division/department committees, organization and/or task forces to make recommendations in the College’s decision-making. Teach assigned courses. Facilitate the classroom instructional process. Evaluate students, monitor progress, and assign final grades in the campus Learning Management System (LMS). Maintain attendance and grade records. Mentor and orient faculty and staff. Maintain required classroom and office hours. Select texts, supplemental documents, equipment, supplies, and other learning resources. Develop supplemental instructional materials. Use current technology in preparation, creation, and delivery of instruction. Create and revise courses and/or curricula as needed. Maintain updated course syllabi. jobs.title: Assistant Professor and Director of Storytelling
jobs.description: Assistant Professor and Director of Storytelling TN, United States Trending Job Description Job Summary The Department of Communication Studies and Storytelling at East Tennessee State University seeks an Assistant Professor and Director of Storytelling. This position carries full-time, tenure-track status beginning August 15, 2026, as an academic year appointment pending continued availability of funds.We seek an energetic and inspiring faculty member with a demonstrated emphasis in Storytelling who will grow our undergraduate programs in Storytelling and our master’s program in Communication and Storytelling Studies through teaching and alliance building with campus and community partners, such as the International Storytelling Center, National Storytelling Network, Mary B. Martin School of the Arts, and Story Collab). Our new colleague should be able to help our students understand storytelling not only as folk and traditional art but also as contemporary practice with socially transformative potential and workplace applications.We are especially interested in candidates who have or are willing to develop an expertise in digital storytelling. The successful candidate must have a demonstrated ability as a performance storyteller and possess strong academic credentials and experience in two or more of the following areas: performance studies; performance ethnography; narrative; oral history, applied storytelling; social justice; street, forum, or interactive theatre; arts-based research methods; storytelling for career preparation (e.g., interpretive biology, public history, environmental or natural resource interpretation, cultural heritage interpretation).Teaching (50%) – The expected teaching load is a 2/3 (two in fall, three in spring) after accounting for a course release to compensate for the service obligations related to directing the Storytelling program. This tenure-track faculty member is expected to teach existing courses to undergraduates (e.g., Introduction to Storytelling, Storytelling Oral Traditions, Telling Personal Stories, Applied Storytelling, Public Speaking, Communication Theory, etc.) and graduate students (e.g., Foundations of Storytelling Performance, Advanced Storytelling Performance, Applied Storytelling, History of Performance Traditions, etc.). Other duties of this position include developing and updating curricula, supervising and mentoring graduate assistants, and assisting with curricular assessments among other duties as assigned. The ideal candidate will also develop new courses, including a course in digital storytelling. This tenure-track faculty member will also advise undergraduate and graduate students, including directing MA theses and/or capstones. The candidate will serve on graduate student M.A. committees and undergraduate honors thesis committees. Teaching formats may include in-person, hybrid, and online teaching. Summer and winter teaching opportunities are optional and available depending on need. All faculty hold regular office hours for students enrolled in classes taught. Service (20-30%) – The successful candidate will direct our Storytelling program in consultation with the department chair. Ideal candidates will demonstrate strong organizational skills, a vision for expanding undergraduate and graduate Storytelling recruitment and programming. Additionally, they will demonstrate the ability to work in collegial and collaborative environments, foster strong ties with local and national storytelling communities, and lead marketing and publicity for Storytelling programming. They will also advise the Storyteller Collective student organization and take the lead in producing storytelling events, including a series of monthly Story Slams. In addition, tenure-track faculty members contribute professional service to the college, university, discipline, and/or community. Research & Creative Activity (20-30%) – Tenure-track faculty contribute to the mission of the Department of Communication Studies & Storytelling through a program of research and/or creative activity that leads to publication, conference presentations, peer-reviewed performances, and/or competitively selected performances. We are particularly interested in candidates whose research agenda connects the Communication Studies and Storytelling programs (e.g., arts-based research methods, performance ethnography, etc.)The Department of Communication Studies & Storytelling serves approximately 100 majors and minors at the undergraduate level and 10 M.A. students. jobs.description: CDL Instructor Columbia, Tennessee, United States Administration Staff Staff Full-Time View favorites The CDL Instructor is responsible for planning, coordinating, and delivering training and instruction for the Commercial Driver License (CDL) program. This is a full time, 12-month, position located on the Columbia, TN Campus. Essential Functions Plan, coordinate, and oversee the CDL program, providing instruction as needed. Participate in recruitment activities at local and regional schools in alignment with the Workforce and Continuing Education Marketing Plan. Schedule and manage training for on-site students, and oversee scheduling, staffing, and observation of training conducted at external partner locations. Coordinate with an approved mechanic to ensure all CDL program vehicles receive required routine, annual, and corrective maintenance. Maintain accurate and up-to-date student records and ensure timely completion of all required FMCSA reporting as well as internal documentation. Develop, implement, and maintain an internal ELDT course to replace the current vendor-provided online version. Represent the CDL program during annual Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security reviews, ensuring compliance with all program standards and addressing any findings or recommendations. Serve as the primary college liaison for CDL-related industry partnerships. Maintain all required program certifications, accreditations, and licensures, as well as a clean driving record. Assist in the selection, evaluation, supervision, and support of temporary and part-time CDL instructors or instructional assistants. Support marketing and outreach efforts with business and industry partners to build and sustain a consistent student and customer base. Maintain regular communication with the Director of Workforce and Continuing Education to report on program operations and identify opportunities to improve quality and efficiency. Support the development and oversight of programs and services that promote enrollment growth, student progression, retention, and successful completion within the service area. Supplemental Functions Support all WCE activities Serve on college committees as directed Education, Training, and Experience Required Unrestricted Class A CDL license Minimum 5 years’ experience with CDL driving Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Ability to communicate effectively in written and spoken English. Ability to establish, coordinate, and implement independent management decisions. Ability to effectively use information technology, including Microsoft Office and related applications. Ability to relate to diverse faculty, staff, students, and the public. Ability to balance workload with multiple tasks. Ability to work without direct supervision. Ability to analyze, evaluate, and take appropriate action. Working Conditions Normal work week of 37.5 hours – 7:45 am – 4:15 pm Monday through Friday. Evening and weekend hours as required. Visual and hand usage for personal computers. Working outdoors in various weather conditions. Driving CDL trucks as needed.
